Projects

Benchmark Cold Plasma System

Medical · 2026 to present

Complete ownership over the whole project. Cold plasma devices for chronic ulcer treatment, ion propulsion, industrial cleaning, etc. Five prototypes, 1.8x performance.

Problem

This technology helps create ion propulsion without additional gas by manipulating the atmosphere. Additionally, it can be used to treat chronic wounds that won't heal due to its biomedical properties.

Solution

An air-ionization mechanism (cold plasma) built from Kapton and copper electrode stacks. Went through various designs and prototypes before managing to create plasma and ion propulsion. Because of the rapid progress I made and the novelty of the technology, I was able to reach out to organizations and eventually establish partnerships with Murata Electronics and GTRI, roughly doubling development speed from access to new technology. Currently I'm creating a miniature pressure control system to increase the plasma generation (plasma forms better in vacuum).

Unexpected challenge

The electrodes had to be thin and safe enough to wear while still producing enough plasma to disrupt biofilm. Additionally, the system had to be light enough to be feasible for various cold plasma/ion propulsion applications.

Rocket Frame Fabrication

Aerospace · 2023 to 2025

Using vacuum bagging, sandwich paneling, male molds, etc. to create various carbon fiber and fiberglass rockets.

Problem

Rockets need to be as light as possible while sustaining mechanical, thermal, and dynamic forces during launch.

Solution

Hundreds of hours of experimentation using different methods to manufacture composite airframes and fins, leading to a 30% reduction in weight.

Unexpected challenge

Controlling the environment during manufacturing and taking extra care during the post-processing and finishing was crucial to ensure the structure wouldn't collapse during launch.

1 / 3

Mechanical Ejection for Altitude Control

Mechanical/Aerospace · 2025

Ejected recovery system based on altitude (instead of standard timed ejection).

Problem

Standard ejections run on time, meaning controlling deployment based on altitude to slow down the rocket or optimize deployment isn't possible.

Solution

Mechanical ejection system that uses a servo, 3D-printed, spring-loaded ejection system, barometer, and microcontroller to eject recovery system.

Unexpected challenge

Puts extreme stress on the rocket, causes heat damage (standard ejection uses hot ejection charge, which has to be rerouted through the rocket to avoid early deployment), and adds multiple failure points. In the end, manipulating the weight of the rocket and its design was much more consistent and reliable for repeated use.

Kite Power Energy Generation (In Progress)

Energy · Research project

Cross-wind kites driving a tether-powered generator.

Problem

Remote and off-grid sites need power without heavy towers or large ground infrastructure.

Solution

The kite flies cross-wind at high speed to raise lift, and the pull on its tether drives an electric generator.

Unexpected challenge

A soft kite has to stay stable and under control at speed to pull hard on the tether.

1 / 2

First Light Dethermalizer

Aerospace · 2023 to 2025

The only deployment-sensing dethermalizer on the market. AKASH sales up 240%.

Problem

Model rockets can drift far on thermals. A dethermalizer ends the flight early to control where the rocket lands.

Solution

A small board with a photoresistor detects deployment and starts the recovery program, with a servo and cage mechanism to act on it.

Unexpected challenge

Every gram counts in a rocket, and the detector board had to weigh under one gram.

1 / 2

Penetrometer

Space · Georgia Tech research project

An embedded penetrometer for soil analysis on the Moon and Mars.

Problem

Landers and future infrastructure need to know whether the ground can carry load, and soil strength is hard to measure remotely.

Solution

A load cell and electronics sit inside the tube. Signal filtering and sensor fusion extract soil properties, and a dashboard sets drop sessions side by side.

Unexpected challenge

Raw readings from a fast drop are noisy, so turning them into soil properties took custom firmware.

PowerWalk

Wearable · 2026

A wearable that returns lost foot sensation. Insole sensors drive haptic motors that map out pressure distribution from the feet onto the calf.

Problem

People who have lost feeling in their feet (neuropathy) cannot sense the ground, which makes every step less stable.

Solution

Sensors in the insole read each footstep. The ESP32 sends that signal to a calf module, which turns it into haptic vibration.

Unexpected challenge

An ESP32, battery, wireless charging coil and pressure sensors all had to fit inside an ordinary slide sandal without changing how it feels to walk.

1 / 3

Spatial Positioning Platform

Game · 2026

IMUs used with sensor fusion algorithm. Sword, shield, and user location communicated through actuators and spatial audio script.

Problem

Military training lacks audio training, which can be crucial to revealing location of threats. This system can also serve to train the blind to find their relative position through spatial audio (from traffic, people, etc.).

Solution

Game style program. An acrylic sword carries an IMU board and battery to track motion with sensory feedback (creating virtual enemies). A shield with an identical setup does the same. Spatial audio tells the player where the enemy is.

Unexpected challenge

A swing or a block had to be sensed and answered with sound fast enough to feel instant, using small, cheap parts. Solved using advanced filtering algorithms (Kalman filter).

1 / 4

Custom Jigs

Manufacturing

Developing custom jigs to assemble more components in-house and faster.

Problem

No hole saw with a 40mm diameter for cutting through foam smoothly; Assembling rocket components requires components to be assembled sequentially, taking far too long; Streamer needs thousands of folds, impossible to do by hand.

Solution

Custom fiberglass holesaw (manufactured through male mandrel) with air holes to blow foam out of holesaw after cutting; Assembly jig to assemble all components at once, drastically reducing cycle time; Custom jig made from modified heatsinks with streamer clamped in between and heated to 200 °C (pleating/heat-setting).

Unexpected challenge

Jigs not only had to perform consistently, but speed, ease of use, and repeated use were just as important.
